scenes.tts: How can two purple-flowered pea plants have a white-flowered offspring? Picture two purple-flowered parents, and between them, one offspring with white flowers. Nothing about the parents' visible color seems to explain it. The answer is hidden inside what each parent carries.
scenes.caption: How can two purple-flowered pea plants have a white-flowered offspring? Picture two purple-flowered parents, and between them, one offspring with white flowers. Nothing about the parents’ visible color seems to explain it. The answer is hidden inside what each parent carries.
scenes.visual: Dark frame. Two large cartoon pea plants fill the left and right thirds. Both have purple flowers. A smaller offspring rises between them and opens a white flower. A cream question mark grows behind it. Plants sway gently throughout. No genotype letters yet. COLOR MAP: purple = P allele and purple phenotype; cream = p allele and white phenotype; teal = sex-cell paths and Punnett grid; gold = prediction; grey = neutral structure.
scenes.narration: How can two purple-flowered pea plants have a white-flowered offspring? Picture two purple-flowered parents, and between them, one offspring with white flowers. Nothing about the parents’ visible color seems to explain it. The answer is hidden inside what each parent carries.

scenes.visual: Brief title card over the same three plants: 'Where Can White Flowers Hide?' The plants keep swaying; the title clears without changing their positions.

scenes.tts: Look inside one parent. Its flower-color gene comes in versions called alleles. This plant carries a purple allele and a white allele. The purple version is dominant, so purple shows. The white version is recessive. It is hidden from view, not damaged or erased.
scenes.caption: Look inside one parent. Its flower-color gene comes in versions called alleles. This plant carries a purple P allele and a white p allele. P is dominant, so purple shows. p is recessive. It is hidden from view, not damaged or erased.
scenes.visual: Camera zooms into the left parent. Two large labelled blocks slide from behind the stem: a purple 'P' block and cream 'p' block. P moves in front and the purple flower glows; p remains fully visible behind, never fading. Small labels 'dominant' and 'recessive' attach to the blocks.
scenes.narration: Look inside one parent. Its flower-color gene comes in versions called alleles. This plant carries a purple P allele and a white p allele. P is dominant, so purple shows. p is recessive. It is hidden from view, not damaged or erased.

scenes.tts: The allele pair a plant carries is its genotype. The flower color that shows is its phenotype. This parent's genotype has one of each allele. Its phenotype is purple. A purple plant can carry a hidden white allele, so appearance alone cannot reveal its pair. Carried information and the visible trait can differ.
scenes.caption: The allele pair a plant carries is its genotype. The flower color that shows is its phenotype. This parent’s genotype is Pp. Its phenotype is purple. A purple plant can carry a hidden p allele, so appearance alone cannot reveal its pair. Carried information and the visible trait can differ.
scenes.visual: The P and p blocks snap together under the label 'genotype: Pp'. Above them, the flower expands under 'phenotype: purple'. A second purple plant slides in with a covered genotype slot marked '?', showing that looks alone do not reveal PP versus Pp.
scenes.narration: The allele pair a plant carries is its genotype. The flower color that shows is its phenotype. This parent’s genotype is Pp. Its phenotype is purple. A purple plant can carry a hidden p allele, so appearance alone cannot reveal its pair. Carried information and the visible trait can differ.

scenes.tts: Before offspring form, the pair separates. Each sex cell carries one allele from the parent. Watch the purple block enter one teal path and the white block enter another. The other parent does the same. Either parent can pass the hidden version onward.
scenes.caption: Before offspring form, the pair separates. Each sex cell carries one allele from the parent. Watch P enter one teal path and p enter another. The other Pp parent does the same. Either parent can pass the hidden p onward.
scenes.visual: Return to both Pp parents. Each Pp pair separates into two large round sex-cell tokens below its plant, one holding P and one holding p. Teal paths carry the tokens toward the centre. Tokens drift slowly while waiting; no molecular structures.
scenes.narration: Before offspring form, the pair separates. Each sex cell carries one allele from the parent. Watch P enter one teal path and p enter another. The other Pp parent does the same. Either parent can pass the hidden p onward.

scenes.tts: A Punnett square organizes those possible meetings. One parent's sex cells settle across the top. The other's settle down the side. Follow a teal path from each edge into a box. The two arriving alleles become one possible genotype for an offspring. Both parents' contributions stay separate and easy to trace.
scenes.caption: A Punnett square organizes those possible meetings. One parent’s sex cells settle across the top. The other’s settle down the side. Follow a teal path from each edge into a box. The two arriving alleles become one possible genotype for an offspring. Both parents’ contributions stay separate and easy to trace.
scenes.visual: The sex-cell tokens transform into headers around a large two-by-two teal grid filling most of the frame. Animated teal paths trace from one top header and one side header into a box. Their allele blocks meet and lock together inside. Keep the parents small at the upper corners.
scenes.narration: A Punnett square organizes those possible meetings. One parent’s sex cells settle across the top. The other’s settle down the side. Follow a teal path from each edge into a box. The two arriving alleles become one possible genotype for an offspring. Both parents’ contributions stay separate and easy to trace.

scenes.tts: Three boxes now hold possible allele pairs. The last box receives the white allele from each parent. What genotype and flower color should appear there? Keep your answer in mind while the paths move.
scenes.caption: Three boxes now hold possible allele pairs. The last box receives p from each parent. What genotype and flower color should appear there? Keep your answer in mind while the paths move.
scenes.visual: Three grid boxes contain PP, Pp and Pp with small purple flowers. The final box is empty. Cream p tokens wait at its top and side. Teal paths pulse toward the empty box. The question remains large above the grid.
scenes.narration: Three boxes now hold possible allele pairs. The last box receives p from each parent. What genotype and flower color should appear there? Keep your answer in mind while the paths move.

scenes.visual: Hold the question and empty final box for thinking. The two cream p tokens glide slowly along their paths but stop just outside the box. Nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: Both white alleles meet. The genotype has two recessive alleles, so the white phenotype appears. The white color never showed in the parents' flowers. It was carried as a hidden allele in each parent, then joined in this offspring.
scenes.caption: Both p alleles meet. The genotype is pp, so the white phenotype appears. The white color never showed in the parents’ flowers. It was carried as a hidden allele in each parent, then joined in this offspring.
scenes.visual: The cream tokens enter and become 'pp'. A white flower grows from that box. A continuous cream trail briefly traces backward from the flower through both p paths to the p blocks inside the parents. Other boxes stay visible but subdued.
scenes.narration: Both p alleles meet. The genotype is pp, so the white phenotype appears. The white color never showed in the parents’ flowers. It was carried as a hidden allele in each parent, then joined in this offspring.

scenes.tts: Now read the whole grid. The allele pairs predict genotypes. The flowers translate them into phenotypes. Most boxes show purple, while one shows white. Each box describes a possible outcome for a new offspring. The grid does not schedule what must happen next.
scenes.caption: Now read the whole grid. The allele pairs predict genotypes. The flowers translate them into phenotypes. Most boxes show purple, while one shows white. Each box describes a possible outcome for a new offspring. The grid does not schedule what must happen next.
scenes.visual: Scan the grid left to right. Genotype labels brighten first, then each flower. A gold bracket labels the purple group and another labels the white box. On-screen only: '3/4 purple', '1/4 white', 'chance for each offspring'. A calendar icon appears, then crosses out under 'not a schedule'.
scenes.narration: Now read the whole grid. The allele pairs predict genotypes. The flowers translate them into phenotypes. Most boxes show purple, while one shows white. Each box describes a possible outcome for a new offspring. The grid does not schedule what must happen next.

scenes.tts: This model has a boundary. It follows one gene, two alleles, one of them dominant, and known parent genotypes. Within that scope, it links what parents carry to what offspring may inherit. Real groups can still vary. For one-gene crosses, Punnett squares predict chances, not exact offspring counts.
scenes.caption: This model has a boundary. It follows one gene, two alleles, one of them dominant, and known parent genotypes. scenes.visual: The grid shrinks slightly inside a clear frame labelled 'one-gene model'. Three scope labels appear around the frame: 'two alleles, one dominant', 'known parent genotypes', 'chance for each offspring'. Small offspring flowers drift below in an uneven sequence to foreshadow variation.
scenes.narration: This model has a boundary. It follows one gene, two alleles, one of them dominant, and known parent genotypes. Within that scope, it links what parents carry to what offspring may inherit. Real groups can still vary. For one-gene crosses, Punnett squares predict chances, not exact offspring counts.
